messages:
dmitri: FYI ran a full host-side perf sweep on canary today, saw a ~12% tail latency regression on small requests after last week's kernel-selection patch. attaching quick notes. :warning:
carla: ugh. is it the batching side or ingress parse?
dmitri: main hotspots are tokenization + request parsing allocations and a lot of tiny writev gRPC frames. flamegraph shows a long tail in host_parse::deserialize -> tokenize::utf8_scan -> writev
ben: can you paste the flame snippet?
dmitri: sure, basic flame (trimmed):
```
--- flame ---
host_parse::deserialize 35%
  tokenize::utf8_scan 18%
  parse_headers 8%
writev (syscall) 12%
grpc::stream_write_smallframes ~10%
kv_cache::lookup_mutex 6%
```
carla: that writev/syscall chunk is suspicious. we coalesced earlier but maybe kernel-selection changed batching patterns so we see many small requests hitting the socket.
eva: KV thrash at 6% — are entries being evicted due to new minibatch behavior?
dmitri: yes, trace suggests we increased minibatch frequency so KV hits drop. also sequences fewer tokens on avg; runtime picked a smaller kernel path which increases host preproc overhead per-token.
alice: any quick repro? or a single-run profile we can use to iterate?
dmitri: repro: run 10k 32-token requests, canary branch kernel-rule-3. Script attached (quick):
```
for i in 1..10000 do
  curl -s -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' $CANARY_URL
done
```
ben: dev hint: try turning on ingress coalescer for grpc: we have an option to buffer up to 4 frames or 4ms, might collapse those writev calls.
carla: also reduce per-request mallocs in parser; there's a known alloc in header canonicalization we can short-circuit for small requests.
eva: for KV: increase kvcache bucket TTL for small requests, or change minibatch sampling to reuse cached prefixes more aggressively. might recover hit rate.
dmitri: tested locally: enabling coalescer saved ~7% p95; bumping kvcache TTL saved ~3%. combined almost back to baseline.
alice: kernel heuristic: can we bias kernel-selection to prefer kernels that trade a bit of device work for lower host preproc? sounds like sequence-length distribution changed and new kernel is host-heavy.
dmitri: exactly. current rule picks kernel strictly on theoretical flops. we need a host-cost term. proposal: kernel_score = flop_score + alpha * host_preproc_cost_est. alpha default 0.2, tunable per-model.
ben: +1. we should derive host_preproc_cost_est from recent request histograms (seq len, tokenization branching).
carla: ops plan? short-term and medium-term?
dmitri: short-term (hotfix):
- enable grpc ingress coalescer on canary (4ms, 8-frame cap)
- bump kvcache tiny-ttl from 60s -> 300s for canary traffic
- disable the new kernel-rule-3 fallback so kernel selection stays on previous path
results: p95 improved ~9% in canary runs
medium-term:
- implement host_cost estimator in kernel selector (use rolling 5m histograms)
- reduce parser allocations: inline header canonicalizer for small requests, reuse buffer pool
- introduce aggressive writev coalescing in proxy (merge small frames pre-serialize)
- add test harness for 1–64 token microbench to prevent regressions
- canary rollout + 24h perf monitor with perf-bot alerts
carla: sounds good. who owns each?
dmitri: I'll push the coalescer + kernel rollback today. carla takeover for parser allocs. ben will handle proxy writev coalesce. eva owns kvcache tuning and canary monitoring. alice will spec the kernel host_cost metric with me.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job: eng-runtime/canary/8812345678 -> runs every 5m for next 6h, alerts on p95 > baseline * 1.05
alice: quick question — for host_cost estimator, do we want tokenization-time per-char or per-token? i vote per-token because UTF branching varies but token boundaries cost is dominant.
dmitri: per-token + small constant per-byte; fine-grained later if needed.
ben: also check HTTP/2 SETTINGS window sizes; we saw some stalls on very bursty clients. increasing initial_window_size by 4k gave small wins in local.
eva: noted. I'll run an A/B with TTL change and window bump.
carla: will open PRs for parser inline and buffer pool, tag them "hot-fix/ingress-allocs"
dmitri: thanks. let's meet 30m to sync after the first canary run. :thumbsup:
